白草原 is the place name Baicaoyuan ("White Grass Plain"); "Baiyuan grasslands" drops 草 and misreads the name.
The Zongge chief Sheqinjiao sought to submit to the court. Zhan sent subordinate general Wang Yongxiang with five thousand cavalry to receive him.
The Zongge chief Sheqinjiao sought to submit to the court. Zhan sent subordinate general Wang Yong with five thousand cavalry to receive him.
The officer is 王詠 (Wang Yong), as s0091 refers to him as 詠; 享 is not part of his name.
Once inside, the Qiang turned on them. Yongxiang sent an urgent dispatch for help, and Wang Hou sent Gao Yongnian to rescue him. They barely escaped.
Once inside, the Qiang turned on them. Yong sent an urgent dispatch for help, and Wang Hou sent Gao Yongnian to rescue him. They barely escaped.
詠 is Wang Yong (王詠); "Yongxiang" is not in the Chinese.
By then Xiazheng had already surrendered, and more than a hundred men, including the Qingtang garrison commander Weixinmuqinzan and his son, were still inside the city.
By then Xiazheng had already surrendered, and only the Qingtang garrison commander Xinmu Qinzhan, his son, and some hundred men remained in the city.
惟 means "only"; it is not part of the name 心牟欽氈 (Xinmu Qinzhan).
Before long Wang Ji, Wei Zhao, and Zhong Pu were defeated and killed in turn, and officers and soldiers lost heart.
Before long Wang Ji, Wei Zhao, and Chong Pu were defeated and killed in turn, and officers and soldiers lost heart.
种樸 uses the surname 种, read Chong, as elsewhere in the chapter (Chong Pu).
An edict banished him to Changhua Army, but on the road at Xiang County he hanged himself.
An edict banished him to Changhua Army, but on the road at Rang County he hanged himself.
穰縣 is Rang County; 穰 is read rang, not xiang.
At the opening of the Chongning era, after Cai Jing became chief councilor, Qian Tong petitioned on behalf of Zhan's achievements;
At the opening of the Chongning era, after Cai Jing became chief councilor, Qian Yu petitioned on behalf of Zhan's achievements;
錢遹 is read Qian Yu; 遹 is pronounced yu, not tong.

and when Wang Hou pacified Shan and Kuo, the court posthumously enfeoffed Zhan as Military Commissioner and Observation Regent of Baoping Army and appointed his son Jue as Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.

and when Wang Hou pacified Shan and Kuo, the court posthumously conferred on Zhan the rank of Military Governor-designate (observation liuhou) of the Baoping Army and appointed his son Jue as Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.
追贈 is a posthumous conferral, not an enfeoffment, and 節度觀察留後 is the liuhou grade below military governor.
Through hereditary privilege he became commander of Jiayuan Fort in Yuan Prefecture and recruited seventeen tribes, including the Qiang chieftain Shuilingbo, totaling eleven thousand tents.
Through hereditary privilege he became commander of Jieyuan Fort in Yuan Prefecture and recruited seventeen tribes, including the Qiang chieftain Shuilingbo, totaling eleven thousand tents.
截原砦 is Jieyuan Fort; 截 is read jie.
He then asked that ancient Wei be made a military prefecture so that Longyou might be secured at its root.
He then asked that Guwei be made a military prefecture so that Longyou might be secured at its root.
古渭 is the place name Guwei (later Tongyuan Army), not "ancient Wei".
Shouyue had also earned merit defending the Hainan and Xiaping regions, yet even that went unrewarded.
Shouyue had also earned merit defending the Hainan and Xianping regions, yet even that went unrewarded.
He was promoted to controller of the Huan-Qing circuit and prefect of Bin, then made deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, Yan-Yan, and Qin-Feng while also holding office as prefect of Kang.
He was promoted to controller of the Huan-Qing circuit and prefect of Bin, then made deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, Fu-Yan, and Qin-Feng while also holding office as prefect of Kang.
鄜延 is the Fu-Yan circuit; 鄜 is read Fu.
His subordinate Xiangya sent an envoy by night with a sword as pledge, offering to bring his forces over in surrender, and Wenyu agreed.
The enemy general Xiangya sent an envoy by night with a sword as pledge, offering to bring his forces over in surrender, and Wenyu agreed.
其將香崖 refers to a general of the Xia enemy who offered to surrender, not Wang Wenyu's own subordinate.
He governed Zhenrong and Deshun armies, took part in securing the Tao and He regions, and was promoted to Left Qilin Vice Commissioner and prefect of Lin.
He governed Zhenrong and Deshun armies, took part in securing the Tao and He regions, and was promoted to Left Qiji Vice Commissioner and prefect of Lin.
左騏驥副使 is the Left Qiji (Thoroughbred Stables) vice commissioner; 騏驥 is not qilin (麒麟).

He served successively as controller of Gaoyang Pass, Ding Prefecture, and the Jingyuan circuit, as prefect of Jing and Bao, and as deputy commander-in-chief of the Ding circuit, and ended his career as Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate.

He served successively as controller of Gaoyang Pass, Ding Prefecture, and the Jingyuan circuit, as prefect of Jing and Bao, and as deputy commander-in-chief of the Ding circuit, and ended his career as Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
東上閣門使 is the Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, not an attendant.
For generations the family had served as inspectors of the frontier tribes. His father, Huai Zhong, held the posts of Inner Hall Honorary Companion and Attendant at the Gate.
For generations the family had served as inspectors of the frontier tribes. His father, Huaizhong, held the posts of Inner Hall Honorary Companion and Attendant at the Gate.
懷忠 is a single given name, Huaizhong; splitting it reads like a surname plus given name.

When Yuan Hao rebelled, he tried to win Huai Zhong over with lavish gifts of gold and silk and the offer of a princely title. Huai Zhong destroyed the seal and beheaded the envoy. When the Xia subsequently invaded, he fought to the death.

When Yuan Hao rebelled, he tried to win Huaizhong over with lavish gifts of gold and silk and the offer of a princely title. Huaizhong destroyed the seal and beheaded the envoy. When the Xia subsequently invaded, he fought to the death.
懷忠 is the given name Huaizhong.
Shaoneng was enrolled in office as Right Squad Palace Guard and granted the imperial surname; he was appointed northern frontier inspector of the army.
Shaoneng was enrolled in office as Right Squad Palace Guard and granted the name Shaoneng; he was appointed northern frontier inspector of the army.
賜以名 means he was granted (this) name; no imperial surname is mentioned.
At Shunning he routed tens of thousands of troops under Dang Yishaliang of the Xia Right Privy Council.
At Shunning he routed tens of thousands of troops under Dang Yishangliang of the Xia Right Privy Council.
黨移賞糧: 賞 is read shang.
For generations the Shaoneng family had served as frontier generals, and the enemy feared them. They repeatedly planted suspicion in hopes of driving a wedge between Shaoneng and the court.
Shaoneng came from generations of frontier generals, and the enemy feared him. They repeatedly planted suspicion in hopes of driving a wedge between Shaoneng and the court.
紹能世世邊將 says Shaoneng (a given name) was of a line of frontier generals; "the Shaoneng family" treats the given name as a family name.

When the Liao of Yu rebelled, the court appointed Xiong Ben pacification commissioner and ordered Inner Treasury Commissioner Yang Wan, Chengdu controller Jia Changyan, Zikui chief inspector Wang Xuan, and Guangzu to join in the punitive campaign, all under Ben's command.

When the Lao tribes of Yu rebelled, the court appointed Xiong Ben pacification commissioner and ordered Inner Treasury Commissioner Yang Wan, Chengdu controller Jia Changyan, Zikui chief inspector Wang Xuan, and Guangzu to join in the punitive campaign, all under Ben's command.
渝獠 are the Lao aboriginal tribes of Yuzhou; "Liao" suggests the Khitan Liao state.
He was promoted to Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate, appointed deputy commander-in-chief, prefect of He, and pacification commissioner of the Taoxi region.
He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, appointed deputy commander-in-chief, prefect of He, and pacification commissioner of the Taoxi region.
東上閣門使 is the Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, not an attendant.

When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Hao was appointed defense commissioner of Zhong, commander of the Pons Day Heavenly Martial Guard, and deputy commander of the horse army; promoted to observation commissioner of Qian; served successively as deputy overall commander of the Fuyan, Taiyuan, Yongxing, and Huanqing circuits; and again became prefect of Lan.

When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Hao was appointed defense commissioner of Zhong, overall commander of the Pengri and Tianwu Guards, and inspector-general (duyuhou) of the Cavalry; promoted to observation commissioner of Qian; served successively as deputy overall commander of the Fuyan, Taiyuan, Yongxing, and Huanqing circuits; and again became prefect of Lan.
捧日天武都指揮使 names the Pengri and Tianwu Guards ("Pons Day" is a garble), and 馬軍都虞候 is the cavalry inspector-general.
He died and was posthumously granted the title of military commissioner of Anhua.
He died and was posthumously granted the rank of military governor-designate (liuhou) of the Anhua Army.
安化軍留後 is the liuhou (designate) grade of the Anhua Army, not a military commissioner.
Luo Shinan of the Fushui tribes attacked Yizhou, and the defending general was killed in battle.
Luo Shinian of the Fushui tribes attacked Yizhou, and the defending general was killed in battle.
羅世念: 念 is read nian.
The tribesmen were routed. Shinan led four thousand eight hundred chieftains and followers in surrendering to the dynasty.
The tribesmen were routed. Shinian led four thousand eight hundred chieftains and followers in surrendering to the dynasty.
The court designed a new long-range Victory Bow pattern capable of piercing armor at three hundred paces and beyond. Border folk called it the "Phoenix Bow."
He submitted a pattern for the Zhisheng long-range bow, capable of piercing armor at three hundred paces and beyond. Border folk called it the "Phoenix Bow."
上 here is the verb "submitted": He Shen presented the bow design; the court did not design it.
He was promoted to governor of Xiang.
He was promoted to Observation Commissioner of Xiangzhou.
相州觀察使 is the Observation Commissioner of Xiangzhou, not a governor of Xiang.
He detached part of his force to serve under Shen as deputy overall commander, who followed Zhong Shidao's army to Baigou and withdrew after twelve days.
Tong Guan detached troops from his command and made Shen deputy overall commander; Shen followed Chong Shidao's army to Baigou and withdrew after twelve days.
Tong Guan made Shen deputy overall commander (the English inverts this), and 种師道 is read Chong Shidao.
He was posthumously honored as Investigating and Pacifying Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wei Su, "Formidable and Stern."
He was posthumously honored as Acting Junior Guardian (jianjiao shaobao) and given the posthumous name Weisu, "Formidable and Stern."
檢校少保 is Acting (jianjiao) Junior Guardian; "Investigating and Pacifying" is a mistranslation.
When Guo Kui and Zhao Jie led the southern campaign, he served as first general.
When Guo Kui and Zhao Xie led the southern campaign, he served as first general.
趙禼: 禼 is read Xie.

The Emperor again sent envoys with rewards, granting him bow, sword, and saddle trappings, ordering his home district corvee duties remitted, promoting him to overall commander of Yan-Yan, and advancing him to deputy overall commander.

The Emperor again sent envoys with rewards, granting him bow, sword, and saddle trappings, ordering his home district corvee duties remitted, promoting him to overall commander of Fu-Yan, and advancing him to deputy overall commander.
He retired with the rank of Left Gold Crow Grand General.
He retired with the rank of Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.
左金吾大將軍 is Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard; "Gold Crow" is a mistranslation of 金吾.
Zhang Shu, military commissioner of Wei, asked his generals who could hold the city. All answered, "Only Guo Cheng will do."
Zhang Jie, military commissioner of Wei, asked his generals who could hold the city. All answered, "Only Guo Cheng will do."
章楶: 楶 is read jie.
Cheng and She Kesui agreed to press the victory with a deep strike. Ten thousand horsemen advanced on separate routes at once and captured the two great chieftains, Amo and Dubo.
Cheng and Zhe Keshi agreed to press the victory with a deep strike. Ten thousand horsemen advanced on separate routes at once and captured the two great chieftains, Amai and Dubu.
折可適 is Zhe Keshi; 阿埋 is Amai and 都逋 is Dubu.
Emperor Shenzong picked him for his martial talent and made him inner-hall assimilated-text commissioner and overall commander of Liyuan Fort in Qingzhou.
Emperor Shenzong picked him for his martial talent and made him Inner Hall Chengzhi and overall supervisor of Liyuan Fort in Qingzhou.
內殿承制 is the rank Inner Hall Chengzhi; "assimilated-text commissioner" is garbled.
The men were stirred to fury. They followed the Quye River some five li, then took position on the north slope of Bollan Ridge. One arrow killed the enemy chieftain, and the host broke in panic.
The men were stirred to fury. They followed the Quye River some five li and took position on Beilanpo Ridge. One arrow killed the enemy chieftain, and the host broke in panic.
北攔坡嶺 is Beilanpo Ridge; "north slope of Bollan Ridge" is garbled.
Qujilin led tens of thousands in boats to camp at Tuokou, threatening Qianjiang city. The garrison had only five hundred men, and panic spread through the town.
Jiling led tens of thousands in boats to camp at Tuokou, threatening Qianjiang city. The garrison had only five hundred men, and panic spread through the town.
犬吉狑 is a split writing of 狤狑 (Jiling); "Qujilin" is not a reading of these characters.
As military control commissioner of Guangxi he was punished for slaughtering surrendered Yao and was demoted to supervising wine taxes at Ji Prefecture.
As military control commissioner of Guangxi he was punished for slaughtering surrendered Yao and was demoted to supervising wine taxes at Jiangzhou.
江州 is Jiangzhou, not Ji Prefecture.
On the campaign against Annan he halted at the Fu River. The other generals hung back, but Yun hitched up his robe, waded across first, and the rest followed.
On the campaign against Annan he halted at the Fuliang River. The other generals hung back, but Yun hitched up his robe, waded across first, and the rest followed.
富良江 is the Fuliang River.
Empress Xiansu's mother, née Zheng, had remarried Yun. Emperor Huizong repeatedly tried to promote him as a favor, but Yun always refused firmly, and people judged him worthy for it.
Empress Xiansu's mother had left the Zheng household and remarried Yun. Emperor Huizong repeatedly tried to promote him as a favor, but Yun always refused firmly, and people judged him worthy for it.
自鄭氏再適 means she left the Zheng household (the empress's father's family) to remarry; it is not her maiden name.
He went out as deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, overseeing the armies of the Qin, Wei, Yan, and Xi circuits, building Xi'an and more than ten forts at Lingyang and Tiandu.
He went out as deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, overseeing the armies of the Qin, Wei, Yan, and Xi circuits, building Xi'an and more than ten forts including Linqiang and Tiandu.
臨羌 is Linqiang, and the two names are examples among the ten-odd forts.
When he fell ill, he retired with the honorary rank of grand preceptor.
When he fell ill, he retired with the rank of Acting Minister of Education (jianjiao situ).
檢校司徒 is Acting (jianjiao) Minister of Education, not grand preceptor.
He died at sixty-two and was posthumously given the honorary title of grand general with ceremonial equivalence to the Three Excellencies.
He died at sixty-two and was posthumously given the title Commander Unequalled in Honour (kaifu yitong sansi).
開府儀同三司 is not a "grand general" title.
His courtesy name was Zhongmou, and he was a kin of Empress Zhanghui.
His courtesy name was Zhongmou; he was a grandson-generation clansman of Empress Zhanghui.
族孫 specifies a clan grandson, not just "a kin".

He was promoted to defense commissioner of Wenzhou, overall commander of the Dragon Spirit and Sun-and-Moon Celestial Martial guards, while remaining deputy overall commander of horse and foot for the circuit.

He was promoted to defense commissioner of Wenzhou and overall commander of the Longshenwei and the Pengri and Tianwu Guards, while remaining deputy overall commander of horse and foot for the circuit.
捧日天武 names the Pengri and Tianwu Guards; "Sun-and-Moon Celestial Martial" is a garble.
Junwan used false accusations to settle scores; Zhan was sly, devious, and hungry for glory. The state has its fixed penalties—father and son condemned to die—and that was only just.
Junwan used false accusations to settle scores; Zhan was sly, devious, and hungry for glory. The state has its fixed penalties—father and son both died in banishment—and that was only just.
謫死 means died in banishment, not "condemned to die".

Name of a bow pattern (weapon), not a person.
Popular name of a bow (weapon), not a person.

Overlong detector span joining the place Iron Mountain to the name; the person Zhao Long is linked separately.

Overlong detector span joining "Even" to the name; Emperor Gaozu of Han is linked separately.

unresolvedReferences.description: 帝 (the emperor) who was alarmed by the revolt is not named; the Qingtang revolt spans the end of Zhezong's reign and the start of Huizong's (AD 1100), so no person link is made.
渭帥 (the commander at Weizhou) who summoned the generals before the Xia attack on Tiansheng Stockade is not named.
宥州監軍 (the Xia military supervisor of Youzhou) who led the iron cavalry toward Songlin Fort is not named.
